body:
## What to build

The reference tells a reader which backends preserve a factor dimension's levels and
ordering, rather than claiming every backend does.

The *Result class and attributes* section currently states that factor and ordered-factor
columns are the one exception to marginplyr not preserving input attributes, and that
their levels and ordering are preserved. It is written without qualification, and
`expand_with_margins()` and the nesting verbs inherit the section as written.

On Arrow it is false under the default Margin label: a factor dimension comes back as a
character column, ordered by its values rather than by its levels. Plain dplyr over the
same Arrow table keeps the dictionary type through `summarise()` and `collect()`, so the
levels are lost by marginplyr rather than by Arrow.

The code is deliberate and already pinned — Arrow can read a schema but cannot restore
factors, because the schema a proxy is built from carries a factor column with no levels
in it — so this is the documentation's claim being wrong, not the behaviour. Two existing
tests assert the character result and one states in a comment that level order is
deliberately not asserted there.

The `.margin_label` section makes the same unqualified claim about reconstruction a second
time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The *Result class and attributes* section names the condition under which levels and
      ordering are preserved instead of claiming it unconditionally, and the claim agrees
      with what the backend capability table actually decides.
- [ ] The second unqualified statement, in the Margin label contract, agrees with the
      first — one of them owns the condition and the other cites it rather than restating
      it.
- [ ] A reader on Arrow can tell from the reference alone what type a factor dimension
      comes back as.
- [ ] Generated documentation is regenerated in the same commit, per *Documentation* in
      `AGENTS.md`.

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.
